title: Elapsed Timer Context Manager

visible.label: Measures positive elapsed duration after block exits
visible.script:
with Timer() as t:
    _ = sum(range(5000))
assert isinstance(t.elapsed, float)
assert t.elapsed >= 0.0

visible.label: Records elapsed even when body raises Exception without suppressing it
visible.inputDisplay: with Timer() as t: raise ValueError("fail")
visible.expectedDisplay: ValueError propagates AND t.elapsed >= 0.0 is populated
visible.script:
t = Timer()
try:
    with t:
        _ = sum(range(1000))
        raise ValueError("fail")
    assert False, "Exception should not be suppressed"
except ValueError:
    pass
assert isinstance(t.elapsed, float)
assert t.elapsed >= 0.0

hidden.label: __enter__ returns self cleanly
hidden.script:
obj = Timer()
with obj as bound:
    assert bound is obj

hidden.label: Reusable across sequential with blocks resets timer cleanly
hidden.inputDisplay: Run same Timer instance twice sequentially
hidden.expectedDisplay: Second run measures cleanly without errors
hidden.script:
t = Timer()
with t:
    _ = sum(range(2000))
e1 = t.elapsed
with t:
    _ = 1 + 1
e2 = t.elapsed
assert e1 >= 0.0 and e2 >= 0.0

hidden.label: Exception return value False behavior

hints: Implement __enter__(self) recording time.perf_counter() and returning self.
Implement __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb) computing time.perf_counter() - self._start and returning False (do NOT return True, which swallows exceptions!).

Pseudocode:
  class Timer:
      def __init__(self, label=""): self.label = label; self.elapsed = 0.0
      def __enter__(self): self._start = time.perf_counter(); return self
      def __exit__(self, *exc): self.elapsed = time.perf_counter() - self._start; return False
